So I've been playing Bringer of Chaos difficulty on Xenoblade 2, coming up to the final battle in Torna the Golden Country before moving on to the base game, and I realised the mode was giving me such a hard time because there was a mechanic I've been ignoring since I never needed it before, that being the Pouch Items. What I used to think was an unnecessary waste of space now becomes a pretty darn useful tool that gives me the edge I need to stand a fighting chance, and it justifies me scavenging and collecting all these field items as they are needed to craft them.

And it really got me thinking, a good topic for an Open Discussion would, what do you think is an ideal way to handle difficulty modes in video games?

There are games like Xenoblade 2, where the difficulty actually changes your way of thinking and encourages you to make use of it's various mechanics to get every advantage you can get on the higher difficulties, while the lower difficulties relax and you have more freedom to play how you like and ignore things that seem like a bother.

There are games like Sonic the Hedgehog series (Before game journalists bitched enough and got rid of multiple playable characters) where the difficulty was more tied to the characters. The level design is the same, but each character had their own abilities and quirks that can either make the level a joke or more difficult than necessary, Like Tails and Cream's ability to fly, and how Knuckles has a lower jump (thank you Sonic Mania for bringing this part of the franchise back btw)

There are games like Megaman Powered Up on the PSP where the difficulty changes the level itself, as I recall on the easier difficulties spikes and bottomless pits are covered up.

There's also the special difficulty modes like Kingdom Hearts Critical Mode or Devil May Cry's Heaven or Hell mode which change the game on a fundamental level with you doing way more damage, but also recieving way more damage, and enemies get way more aggressive, it requires a different mindset entirely.

And lastly there are games like most shooters where all they really do is just the enemies become bullet sponges but can kill you by sneezing.

I'd like to know if there's other interesting approaches to difficulty modes you guys have encountered that I don't know about.
